title: Derived scalar extension under the constructed relative coefficient transport
statement: Let g:Y→X be a scheme morphism, let B,R be commutative rings in the site universe, and let f:B→R be a ring homomorphism. Native derived scalar extension from B_X to R_X followed by inverse image to Y and relativeFiniteModelDerived(g,R) is naturally isomorphic to inverse image to Y followed by relativeFiniteModelDerived(g,B) and adicFiniteExtension(f) on the equivalent small site. This is a functor isomorphism, with no cohomological or finiteness hypothesis.

proof.text: Use K-flat resolutions and preservation of quasi-isomorphisms to construct a derived adjunction for small-site change of rings. Its left-derived universal property identifies the left adjoint with the recorded adicFiniteExtension. Compose this and the native scalar-extension adjunction with the transport equivalences. The right adjoints are identified by the derived restriction square, so uniqueness of left adjoints gives the comparison. Finally compose with the native pullback/scalar comparison.

theorem relativeFiniteScalarTransport {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ X)
    {B R : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing B] [CommRing R] (f : B →+* R) :
    Nonempty ((pbcDerivedExtend ((constantSheaf (ProEt.topology X)
        CommRingCat.{u + 1}).map (CommRingCat.ofHom f)) ⋙
      adicTowerPullback g (adicLisseConstantRing X R) ⋙ relativeFiniteModelDerived g R) ≅
      (adicTowerPullback g (adicLisseConstantRing X B) ⋙
        relativeFiniteModelDerived g B ⋙
          adicFiniteExtension (proEtaleModelTopology Y) f))
